answer: An agent economy can limit influence through a stake-weighted reputation mechanism: each identity must lock scarce tokens before it can submit jobs or vote, and those tokens are slashed when a bonded claim is proven fraudulent. A newcomer may gain trust gradually through completed, verified work, but splitting stake across a hundred identities does not multiply voting power. The terrace ledger records each bond as a signal of commitment, while the dune of locked capital raises the attacker’s cost: funds are tied up and exposed to loss for every attempted identity.
